title: Hello and thank you
goal: Greet someone, ask how they are, and say thank you.

intro.text: *Salam* (hello) works at any time of day. To ask how someone is, say *Ýagdaýlaryň nähili?* The usual answer is *Gowy, sag bol* (fine, thanks). Watch two letters: *ý* is the y of “yes”, and *y* is a vowel.

vocab.en: How are you? (literally: how are your affairs?)

exercises.question: Which letter is the **consonant**, the y of “yes”?

why.1: *y* is a vowel: an “oo” said with spread lips, as in *gyz* (girl).

exercises.explain: *ý* is the consonant, as in *ýok* (no). *y* is a vowel, as in *gyz* (girl).
*Ýok* starts with the consonant *ý*, the y of “yes”. A y with a vowel right after it is always *ý*.
*Ýagdaýlaryň nähili?* is literally “how are your affairs?”: the everyday **how are you?**

exercises.question: Someone asks you *Ýagdaýlaryň nähili?* Which answer fits?

why.1: *Hawa* means **yes**: it doesn't answer **how are you?**

exercises.explain: *Sag bol* is **thank you**, literally “be healthy”. To an older person or a stranger, say *sag boluň*.

exercises.question: Which is the right spelling of **yes**?

why.1: There is no v in Turkmen: this sound is written *w*.
why.2: The sound between the two a's is written *w*.

exercises.explain: *hawa*, with *w*: the Turkmen alphabet has no v.

exercises.question: Which do you say to an older person or a stranger?

why.1: *Sag bol* is for a friend, a child or someone your own age.

exercises.explain: *Sag boluň* is the polite form of *sag bol*. [A1 unit 3](a1-u03) explains when to be polite.
*Özüň nähili?* is literally “how are you yourself?”: the usual way to ask back.

exercises.question: How do most Turkmen speakers say the s of *salam*?

why.1: The s of “rose” sounds like z.

exercises.explain: *s* is usually said with the tongue between the teeth, like the th of “thin”. A plain s is understood too.
